caption:
Missing image descriptions: the single biggest accessibility failure we found.

1,179 pages across 13 public Confluence sites. 1,765 images with no alt text, scattered across 311 pages.

An image that should explain a step becomes invisible to a screen reader. "Image" is all it says.

Not a hard fix — one paragraph per slide — but it compounds across a space: you can't explain screenshots with pictures. You need words.

Method, data, and limits: clearwren.com (link in bio).

#WebAccessibility #A11y #AltText #DigitalAccessibility #WCAG #Confluence #Documentation

slides.label: What a screen reader hears
slides.headline: Just the word image.
slides.body: A user who cannot see the screenshot has no idea what step it was meant to show. The information is gone.
slides.alt: What a screen reader hears: just the word image. A user who cannot see the screenshot has no idea what step it was meant to show. The information is gone.

slides.label: How to fix it
slides.headline: One paragraph per image.
slides.body: Describe what the screenshot shows: the button you clicked, the tab that opened, the state of the page. That paragraph becomes the alt text.
